title: 1b — Telling Stories with Python

content.title: Strings are text
content.summary: Anything inside quotes is a string — Python displays it exactly as written.
content.body: In Python, any text inside quotes is called a string. Strings can contain letters, numbers, spaces, punctuation — even emoji! Python will display them exactly as you type them.

content.title: Multiple print statements
content.summary: Each print() puts its message on a new line — write as many as you like.
content.body: You can have as many print() lines as you like. Each one puts its message on a new line in the output. Programs are like a list of instructions — Python follows them one by one.

content.title: Programs run top to bottom
content.summary: Python always starts at line 1 and reads down — order matters.
content.body: Python always starts at the first line and works its way down. The order you write your print() lines is the order they appear in the output.

starterCode:
print("A dragon appeared!")
print("You found a sword.")
editorPrompt: Write a short story using multiple print() lines — one line per print().
